Synthesis and application of isoindigo quaternary
ammonium salts in copper plating
Ruiqi Shan, Chenhao Qian, Xuyang Li, Xin Chen and Limin Wang *
Received 30th April 2025,
Accepted 5th August 2025
Achieving uniform through-hole filling by copper electrodeposition is important for the fabrication of
printed circuit boards (PCBs), and the development of suitable additives is a key process to realize
eficient electrodeposition. Five isoindigo (IID) quaternary ammonium salts were synthesized using
isoindigo molecules as the core skeleton. Electrochemical tests, theoretical calculations, and molecular
dynamics simulations demonstrated that the isoindigo derivatives have the ability to act as leveler and
exhibit electrode absorption capacity, among which IID-C4-QL showed the best inhibition of copper
deposition as well as the best cathodic adsorption ability The high through-hole filling and excellent
leveling performance of IID-C4-QL were confirmed by actual electroplating tests.

3. Results and discussion
3.1. Cyclic voltammetry measurements
Cyclic voltammetry is one of the commonly used methods for
analyzing the inhibitory efect of additives on metal electro-
deposition.<sup>24</sup> The negative peak in the curve represents the
cathodic reduction peak of copper ions, while the positive peak
represents the anodic stripping peak of copper. The peak areas
in the copper deposition zone and the copper stripping

and the stripping amount of metallic copper, respectively,
and these two quantities are directly proportional.<sup>25</sup> Therefore,
the deposition of copper ions is represented by the positive
peak area, and the smaller the positive peak area, the stronger
the inhibitory efect of the additive on copper ion deposition.<sup>26</sup>

4. Conclusions
In summary, five isoindigo quaternary ammonium salt deriva-
tives were synthesized in this paper using isoindigo as the
parent body to explore their application as levelers in PCB
through-hole plating. The results of electrochemical experi-
ments show that five IID-QAS exhibit diferent degrees of
copper deposition inhibition, among which IID-C4-QL has the
best inhibition performance and strong convective adsorption
ability. Theoretical calculations and molecular simulations
show that IID-C4-QL has the strongest adsorption capacity
among the five compounds. In the actual copper plating test,
the highest TP value of 120.77% can be obtained with the
addition of IID-C4-QL at 1.5 ppm, and the SEM results show
that IID-C4-QL can obtain the flattest layer at the same concen-
tration, while the addition of more than 1.5 ppm will compete
with SPS for adsorption, resulting in the ‘‘cavity phenomenon’’
and decrease of the TP value of the layer. XRD results show that
the addition of IID-C4-QL transforms the crystallographic
orientation of the copper layer from (220) to the most stable
(111) crystallographic plane. The present work enriches the
study of isoindigo on this field and exploits the great potential
and scope of isoindigo derivatives for acid plating applications.
